title: Committed app.bin (2 MB executable) — a build artifact tracked at the repo root
evidence: chunk-6-misc.patch: 'diff --git a/app.bin b/app.bin / new file mode 100755 / Binary files /dev/null and b/app.bin differ'; worktree: 'git ls-files' lists app.bin, 'ls -la app.bin' -> '-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 moses staff 2057480  9 Aug 15:47 app.bin'; '.gitignore' adds only 'tools/raylib-sw/ bin/ goldens/_reports/'; README.md: 'odin build app          # produce the binary'
detail: A 2 MB platform-specific executable is tracked at the root, added by the head commit; .gitignore covers bin/ but not app.bin. It bloats the repo, is non-portable, and silently drifts from the tree.
recommended_fix: git rm --cached app.bin, add '/app.bin' (or '*.bin') to .gitignore, and let CI's 'odin build app' step produce the artifact.

title: data/crises.json is parsed and hashed but never consumed — tuning it is a no-op that forces a golden re-bless
evidence: core/catalog.odin:315-333 parses it ('v, e := json.parse(src.crises, parse_integers = true)' ... 'cd.lead_time_ticks = jint(eo, "lead_time_ticks", 0)'); catalog.odin:153 'mix(&h, src.crises)' hashes it; grep for 'lead_time_ticks'/.crises across core/app/harness returns only loader/testkit hits; core/crisis.odin:8 'the surge is forecast by the catalog timeline' (demand.json set_pieces), Crisis_Def fields read by nothing
detail: lead_time_ticks (600) and preventive_redesign are dead data: the surge lifecycle comes from demand.json. Editing crises.json changes catalog_hash, so all T1 manifests fail 'catalog drift' for a behavior no-op — the loaded-but-never-applied shape from prior rounds.
recommended_fix: Consume lead_time_ticks/preventive_redesign in the crisis/forecast path, or trim crises.json to fields the sim reads; stop hashing catalog bytes that cannot change behavior.
